Title I Reporting of Eligible Students

12 PM, Virtual

ESEA Coordinators, please share the following information with your non-public contacts!

Non-public schools who wish to receive Title IA equitable services in FY28 must attend the Title I Reporting of Eligible Students webinar on September 1, 2026 at 12:00pm. This webinar will review reporting requirements and processes. After the training, the recording will be available on the DOE Data YouTube Playlist.

To be eligible for FY28 Title IA equitable services, Non-Public School Officials must submit student data into Connect by October 1, 2026.

Spotlight Title I Family Engagement Title I Parent and Family Engagement Requirements

Parent's Right to Know
As part of Title I, Part A, SAUs and schools must implement important family engagement practices, including sending the “Parent’s Right to Know” within the first four weeks of school, which should be a letter that notifies parents of their right to know:

  • Professional qualifications of student’s teachers and paraprofessionals
  • State/local assessment policies
Please review the general outline of a "Parent's Right to Know" requirement. The notice can also be posted in the student handbook and/or on the SAU/School website.

Title I Annual Meeting
Every Title I school must convene parents, at least annually, to explain the program and solicit parent feedback. For Title I Schoolwide programs, these meetings are at the whole-school level. For Targeted Assistance Programs, it's a requirement for the Title I Teacher to meet the identified students' parents and to inform of their students' participation and solicit feedback.

School-Parent Compacts
Title I Family Engagement policies should be updated annually with the involvement of parents. This includes the school-parent compact. The Title I School-Parent Compact  addresses the importance of communication between teachers and parents on an ongoing basis through, at a minimum— 
  • parent-teacher conferences in elementary schools, at least annually, during which the compact shall be discussed as the compact relates to the individual child’s achievement
  • frequent reports to parents on their child(ren)’s progress
  • reasonable access to staff, opportunities to volunteer and participate in their child’s class, and observation of classroom activities; and 
  • ensuring regular two-way, meaningful communication between family members and school staff, and, to the extent practicable, in a language that family members can understand
 

 

Read More about Title I Family Engagement Requirements
Update Title I Summer Grant Title I Summer Performance Report Available on September 8 and Due October 16

The Title I Summer Grant will have a Performance Report that will be live on September 8. SAUs will have till October 16 to complete it. Because the start of the school year is very busy, I wanted to make sure I shared steps that should be completed prior to the Performance Report:

  • Necessary budget adjustments have been made to enable invoicing.
  • All invoicing has been completed.
  • Student outcomes on goals and best practices are analyzed.

 

Spotlight Maine's Model of School Support

FY 25 SIG funds are expiring for all identified schools and need to be obligated by 9/30/26 and invoiced for reimbursement by 12/15/26. FY 26 SIG funds are expiring for schools that exited CSI status in January 2026 and need to be obligated by 9/30/26 and invoiced by 12/15/26. Obligations and invoices should align with submitted CSI exit plans for each exiting school.

Schools continuing in CSI status for SY2026-2027 will continue to have access to FY 26 SIG funds due to the granting of a Tydings waiver.

Continuous School Improvement resources are available on the Maine Department of Education-ESEA Federal Programs webpage. To access resources and SIG Application training videos, visit our Continuous School Improvement Resources on the ESEA Guidance page under Continuous School Improvement-Title I Section 1003.

Fiscal Corner

Update Tyra is Out on Vacation

Tyra is out on vacation from August 28-September 8, and the normal turnaround times will be implemented upon her return. She will review invoices in the order they were received within two weeks of the date the request was submitted.

News Friendly Reminders! Invoicing and Approval

Time and Effort documentation will be required with the first invoice for the FY 27 grant where reimbursement is being requested for salaries and benefits. This is to develop a collection process for all DOE federal grants. ESEA is doing our best to align to other federal grant programs within the department. This documentation will be the latest that SAU has on file. Please keep in mind if your SAU uses a template that requires an attached schedule then make sure the schedule is uploaded as well.

Requesting reimbursement for expenses related to a schoolwide plan; you must code the expenses on the invoice side of Grants4Me appropriately. Funds used to support the schoolwide plan in the application are not budgeted out into object codes and function codes.

Accrued expenses at the end of a fiscal year cannot be paid using new funds. For example, the salaries and benefits that were just accrued to close out the FY 26 year cannot be reimbursed using FY 27 funds. Accrued salaries and benefits cannot be reimbursed until they are paid out.

Subscriptions must fall within the period of performance for the grant and reimbursement cannot be requested until after payment has been made for the subscription and the start date has passed.

Reimbursement requests for travel, PD conference registrations, tuition, supplies, etc. must be accompanied by an invoice or receipt for the expense. This cannot be a PO or reimbursement voucher form from the SAU.

News Contractual Services

Contractual Services
Please be mindful of what determines an obligation per the Code of Federal Regulations 76.707. Contracts cannot be obligated for new funds (FY 27) until after the substantial approval date. The services received must fall within the period of performance for the grant. Most Federal grant’s period of performance starts upon substantial approval of the application for funds. Federal funds cannot reimburse contract deposits for service.

notes: 1 section header — too few for a contents list.
Heading levels skip: jumps h1 to h4. Needs a person.
1715 words with no section headers at all — the biggest single improvement available here.

decisions.label: Rebuild the heading outline
decisions.why: 4 headings sit at a level the page never opens — "ESEA Office Hours" is an h4 with no h3 above it, so it is neither announced nor styled as the sub-section it is. Each heading moves to one level below whatever encloses it.

decisions.label: Write the email addresses the same way
decisions.why: 6 addresses are shown in whatever case it was typed in. The house form capitalises each name and leaves a middle initial in lower case — jessica.s.caron@maine.gov → Jessica.s.Caron@maine.gov. Only the first letter of each part changes, so a name that spells itself LaBreck keeps doing so.

decisions.label: Give the sub-headings their rule
decisions.why: 5 sub-headings are plain bold text. The design has a treatment for them — a teal rule down the left and a line across — and it had never been used on any page, because it needs a wrapper an author would have to know about.

decisions.label: Draw a closing link as the action it is
decisions.why: 1 passage ends with a paragraph holding nothing but a link — the thing the passage was leading up to. Set as running text it looks like any other link in the sentence above it. The site already has one way of drawing an action, so it takes that. The words do not change.

decisions.label: Make a loose address look like an address
decisions.why: 7 email addresses sit in the body of this page rather than in a contact block, drawn exactly like every other link — so the one that opens a mail window looks the same as the ones that go to web pages. The chip carries the same envelope the banner's contact link uses. The address itself does not change.

decisions.label: Size an image by its shape
decisions.why: "Maine Department of Education" could not be measured, so it is floated left and capped rather than left at its own size.

decisions.label: Drop the endorsement disclaimer
decisions.removes: Links to organizations and resources are for reference and information only and do not imply endorsement by the Maine Department of Education.
decisions.why: The same sentence appears verbatim on six pages and is true of every page on the site, which is why it is moving to the footer. Matched in full and in one exact form — nothing near it is touched.

decisions.label: Stop a picture floating with nothing beside it
decisions.why: 1 picture is set to float so text runs up beside it, but what follows it is a grid, a card or a table — a box, which clears the float rather than wrapping. So the picture sits alone with a column of white to its right and everything below starts past the bottom of it. Unfloated it is a picture in the flow, which is what it already looked like.
